name: Blue-and-white ceramic / porcelain decoration
material: ceramic body decorated with cobalt pigment, generally under a transparent glaze; body/firing technology varies by culture and period
fabrication_process: paint cobalt decoration on prepared body
fire so decoration and glaze become materially integrated
visible_production_marks: brush-loaded cobalt lines vary in width/density
bleeding or pooling can occur through body/glaze interaction
edge_behavior: Painted edges are brush-made and slightly integrated into glaze/body; decoration must wrap geometry rather than float as a 2D decal.
mark_making: brush-loaded cobalt lines vary in width/density
bleeding or pooling can occur through body/glaze interaction
color_behavior: Restricted blue/white logic with cobalt density variation; firing may shift intensity; reserve white is active negative space.
surface_behavior: Glazed ceramic has hard specular highlights over painted underglaze; foot/rim may reveal body and firing evidence.
composition_behavior: Design motifs around object zones—rim, neck, shoulder, belly, foot, well—and use rotational/radial balance appropriate to form.
structural_limitations: do not render decoration above glaze like vinyl stickers
not every blue-and-white tradition equals Ming Jingdezhen
aging_weathering: glaze crazing/staining only when state supports it

prompt_fragments.core: Treat the image as cobalt brush decoration fused beneath a transparent glaze: blue density varies with brush load, motifs follow the ceramic curvature, glaze reflections sit above the painting, and object zones structure the composition.

typical_generation_failures: flat poster shaped like a vase
Ming motifs automatically imported into Edo case
evaluation_criteria: glaze and ceramic body remain distinct layers
cultural motif family matches requested context

sources.supports: cobalt-blue pigment on white body, brush application under transparent glaze, Jingdezhen history

scope_note: This module controls material/production behavior. It does not select an era by itself.
